subject: Harmonize tenor + staggered uplift checklist for Acme renewal
messages:
From: Lydia Parker <lydia.parker@acme-analytics.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal discussion — intent to move to multi-year + staggered uplift

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the Q1 usage summary — the team ran the numbers and we think a longer-term structure makes sense. High level: Acme wants to move to a 36-month commitment to lock in price stability, but we need a staged ramp so we can scale capacity in line with product launches (Aug 2027 and Feb 2028).

Key asks:
- 3-year term, co-term with our fiscal July start if possible
- Year 1: 40% of expected run-rate, Year 2: 75%, Year 3: 100% (we're open to front-loaded credits to offset onboarding)
- An auto-renew clause unless we provide 60 days notice
- Clear overage treatment and canary/fallback to a smaller model variant if capacity constrained

Procurement wants a mutual action plan and a draft amendment to review. Attaching our internal forecast (high level) as .xlsx. Can your team put together a staged-commit checklist and a suggested amendment we can circulate to legal?

Appreciate it — Lydia

Attachments: Acme_MAAP_Usage_Q1.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Lydia Parker <lydia.parker@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 13:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — intent to move to multi-year + staggered uplift

Hi Lydia — thanks for the clear asks and the forecast. We're aligned on the high-level structure and can operationalize the staged ramp while preserving SLA/backstop behavior.

I sketched a short mutual action plan below and attached a one-page checklist for your procurement/legal teams. High-level proposal:
- Term: 36 months, start 2027-07-01 to line up with your fiscal window (co-term).
- Staggered commit: Year1 = 40% of target tokens, Year2 = 75%, Year3 = 100%. We will support a one-time frontloaded credit to accelerate onboarding equivalent to ~10% of the three-year committed spend, applied in Year1.
- Auto-renew: 12-month auto-renew unless either party gives notice 60 days before renewal window. We can include a annual true-up mechanism.
- Capacity fallbacks: define model-variant fallback and routing policy in Appendix A (e.g., shift to a compatible quantized variant with preserved prompt behavior).
- Billing: quarterly invoices; true-ups at each annual boundary with line-item for applied credits.

Next steps I propose:
1) Redwood sends draft amendment + Appendix A (routing/fallback + SLO credit) — target EOD Tue 6/8.
2) Acme legal/proc shares redlines by Thu 6/10.
3) Finalize commercial amendment + procurement signoff by Fri 6/18 to hit July 1 start.

I've looped in Marissa (Sales Lead) and Karthik (Sales Ops) to finalize the amendment and the DocuSign flow. If the procurement calendar is tighter we can compress the timeline; tell me what dates don't work.

Thanks,
Sean
Senior Account Exec | Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0132

Attachment: Draft one-page checklist (sent inline)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Lydia Parker <lydia.parker@acme-analytics.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — intent to move to multi-year + staggered uplift

Thanks, Sean / Lydia. Per Sean's plan, attaching the draft amendment (3YR, staged ramp) with two commercial options: (A) standard frontloaded credit (10% of committed spend) + quarterly true-up OR (B) higher up-front credit (15%) with a modest price ladder tied to uplift.

Legal/Billing notes to call out for Acme:
- We need explicit language for the "staged commit" percentages and the mechanics for annual true-up.
- Define overage: usage beyond committed tokens billed at list overage rate with a 30-day invoice buffer.
- Canary fallback: we add explicit rollback trigger conditions (regional capacity < X for > 5 mins) and SLA credit schedule if fallback occurs.
- DocuSign flow: Redwood executes the amendment; Acme countersigns. We can preset the invoice schedule in the DocuSign manifest.

I've attached Draft_Amendment_3yr-StaggeredRamp_20270607.docx. Marissa

Attachment: Draft_Amendment_3yr-StaggeredRamp_20270607.docx (docx)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Lydia Parker <lydia.parker@acme-analytics.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2027 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — intent to move to multi-year + staggered uplift

Quick ops note and timeline check:
- I'll create the HubSpot amendment record (Deal RWD-ACME-2027-045) and attach both the Acme forecast and our draft amendment.
- DocuSign envelope is ready to go once Acme confirms the commercial option (A or B) and the fiscal start date (we're holding July 1 as proposed).
- Billing: we'll instruct finance to set quarterly invoices with the first invoice pro-rated for July. If Acme wants monthly true-ups instead of annual, we can support that but it will change the billing cadence and possibly the applied credit calculation.

Lydia — can you confirm: 1) preferred credit option (A/B), and 2) that procurement can return redlines by Thu 6/10 EOD? If you prefer, we can hop on a 20-minute call tomorrow to walk legal through the amendment.

Thanks — Karthik
Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
